papers.title_en: MX-Like Tensor Core for LLM Inference with NPU Integration via Hardware-Software Co-Design Exploration
papers.authors: Zijun Zhao, Ruichu Ao, Stef Cuyckens, Marian Verhelst, Chao Fang
papers.evidence: 面向LLM推理的MX与NVFP4等块缩放量化格式
papers.tldr: MX/NVFP4类块缩放量化在NPU边缘LLM推理中的设计空间尚未系统探索，精度与硅成本权衡不清。本文定义完整8位缩放格式族与非对称权重-激活精度，构建按格式特化的MAC模板，并将自动化软硬件协同流程集成到开源SNAX NPU。结果显示缩放格式仅在激进FP4下显著影响精度；UE5M3在FP4区间较NVFP4-like基线困惑度退化最多降25.3%，面积仅增0.06%、功耗增0.49%。
papers.abstract_en: Block-scaled quantization formats such as OCP Microscaling (MX) and NVFP4 have been widely adopted as efficient data formats for LLM inference. However, the design space of these formats spanned by shared scale, weight, and activation format combinations has not been systematically explored, and the joint accuracy-silicon tradeoff across this space remains uncharacterized, leaving the true Pareto-optimal configurations for NPU-based edge LLM deployment an open question. To bridge this gap, we conduct a joint hardware-software (HW-SW) co-design exploration of the above underexplored MX-like design space with three innovations. 1) We define and systematically characterize the full 8-bit scale format family within the MX-like design space, jointly with asymmetric weight-activation precision, identifying configurations that outperform the MX and NVFP4-like (without per-tensor scaling, PTS) baselines. 2) We build a per-format specialized MAC datapath template that enables fair hardware cost evaluation across the space. 3) We develop an automated co-design flow, integrated into the open-source SNAX NPU platform, that enables joint HW-SW analysis across the design space. Overall, our co-design exploration reveals that scale format matters only under aggressive FP4 quantization, yielding a case-oriented design guideline for both scale format and asymmetric weight-activation precision. We further identify UE5M3 as a favorable accuracy-hardware tradeoff for the FP4 regime, reducing perplexity degradation by up to 25.3% relative to the NVFP4-like baseline, at a cost of only +0.06% area and +0.49% power overhead.

papers.title_en: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
papers.authors: Feiyang Hong, Yujie Wei, Bo Zhao, Xiu Su, Hongxun Yao, Shuo Yang
papers.evidence: 将多帧视觉历史压缩为紧凑槽位并保留时序线索
papers.tldr: 机器人操作常依赖短暂接触、遮挡与中间状态等短期线索，单帧难以消歧。CondenseVLA 在多帧 VLA 解码端引入可学习历史压缩模块，用查询和交叉注意力把缓存帧特征蒸馏为固定槽 token，并用辅助正则减少槽间冗余。它在 Simpler-WidowX 将成功率从 58.7% 提至 69.8%，LIBERO 达 97.2%，真实任务达 52.8%。结果表明选择性压缩近期视觉证据有助于动作解码，但困难多观测任务仍受有限历史窗口限制。
papers.abstract_en: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. We propose CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding. Given a sequence of cached per-frame features from the VLM backbone, CondenseVLA distills observation history into a fixed set of slot tokens using learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention. Simple auxiliary regularization penalizes overlap among slot attention maps and decorrelates slot embeddings, encouraging complementary attention and reducing slot redundancy. Across the evaluated tasks, CondenseVLA improves Simpler-WidowX success from 58.7% to 69.8% (+11.1 percentage points), achieves 97.2% on LIBERO, and reaches 52.8% on real-world tasks. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA
